title: Agent text can carry links with a hover popup and a click that opens the target through decade
body:
Agent text reaches coax as markdown and is drawn through cmr. cmr leaves links (`[text](url)`) as typed, and the coax output style tells the model not to write them. Nothing in a reply is interactive. coax already captures the mouse, so it knows where the pointer is and what was clicked, and it holds a socket to decade (`connect_decade` in `src/app.rs`). decade's protocol has `show`, `highlight` and `clear` verbs, each naming a kind such as `file`, delivered to the pane that shows that kind.

Jack wants coax to define its own link form, with two behaviours:

- Hovering a link opens a popup with more about its target.
- Clicking a link sends an open command over the decade channel.

Use cases he named:

- Hovering a foam issue ID shows the issue's description.
- Clicking a file path opens the file in whatever decade pane shows files.

This needs serious design before any code.

## Open

- The syntax. Candidates: plain markdown links with coax-specific schemes, as in `[coax-12e8af](foam:coax-12e8af)` and `[src/ui.rs:40](file:src/ui.rs#40)`; a bracket form of coax's own, as in `[[foam:coax-12e8af]]`; or no syntax at all, with coax recognising issue IDs and paths in plain text. The model has to be taught whichever wins, through the coax output style (coax-3d286f).
- Where hover content comes from. For a foam issue, coax could run `foam show --json`. A general answer could be link kinds defined in `config.toml`, each with a command whose output fills the popup. Whatever the answer, a slow or failing provider must not stall drawing.
- What a click sends. `show` with kind `file`, target the path and `at` the line fits decade's existing verb for files. Other kinds may need verbs decade does not have yet, and decade-channel is still changing.
- What happens with no decade connection, or no pane that shows the kind: a dim notice, or the link drawn as plain text.
- How links render: colour, underline, and whether cmr learns the syntax or coax handles it on top of cmr's rows.
- Whether link kinds are fixed in coax or come from config, given that coax is meant to stay agent-generic.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4d38e22a
notes.text: Text colouring by palette name is filed separately and also needs an inline syntax of coax's own. The two should share one form; see that issue's open questions.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4d38e22a
notes.text:
Landed in 7a387c5 on dev, with the form settled by Jack's approval: plain markdown links, with coax giving each scheme its meaning. cmr parses the link and draws it underlined. coax reads the scheme and nothing coax-specific is in cmr.

- `color:<name>` draws the text in that palette colour, with no hover and no click. This answers coax-ec0448 as well.
- `file:<path>#<line>` is blue and underlined. Hover shows the relative path, the line and the title. A click sends decade `show` with kind `file`, the absolute path and the line, to `[links] decade_pane` (default `code`). With no connection the line under the prompt says `no decade connection`.
- `http:` and `https:` show the URL on hover. A click runs `xdg-open` only with `[links] open_urls = true`.
- `foam:` and any scheme under `[links.schemes.<scheme>]` run a configured `hover` argv on hover, with a 2 s limit, and cache the output per target. An optional `click` argv runs detached.

Left for Jack:

- The scheme names (`color:`, `file:`, `foam:`) and the coax output style wording that teaches the model to write them (coax-3d286f).
- `open_urls` defaults to false. I lean to leaving it false until the output style tells the model to link URLs, since a model that is prompt-injected could otherwise put a link in front of you.
- Links inside a code block or a table wider than the screen draw but have no hover or click, because those blocks pan by columns.
- A hover target that starts with `-` runs nothing, so a link cannot pass a flag to the configured command.
- Close both issues when the human-facing parts are decided. I closed neither.
